title: 🎯 Welcome to Units & Measurements

sections.heading: Why This Chapter Matters
sections.body:
Physics is built on measurement. Every physical quantity — speed, force, energy — needs a NUMBER and a UNIT to be meaningful.

"The distance is 5" means nothing.
"The distance is 5 metres" is physics.

sections.heading: What You'll Learn
sections.body:
• What physical quantities are and how they're classified
• The 7 SI base units and why they exist
• How to derive units of any quantity
• Dimensional analysis — the most powerful tool in this chapter
• Significant figures, errors, and precision

highlight: This topic carries 1–2 questions in JEE Main every year. Dimensional analysis alone can solve MCQs in seconds!

title: Physical Quantities — The Foundation

sections.heading: What is a Physical Quantity?
sections.body:
A physical quantity is any property of matter or energy that can be measured and expressed as a number with a unit.

Examples: mass, length, time, temperature, electric current.

sections.heading: Two Types
sections.body:
1. Fundamental (Base) Quantities — cannot be expressed in terms of other quantities. They are the building blocks.

2. Derived Quantities — expressed as combinations of fundamental quantities.

Example: Speed = Distance / Time = (Length) / (Time) → derived from two fundamental quantities.

highlight: There are exactly 7 fundamental quantities in the SI system. Everything else in physics is derived from them.

question: Which of the following is a fundamental (base) physical quantity?
explanation: Electric current (ampere) is one of the 7 SI base quantities. Velocity = length/time (derived), Force = mass×acceleration (derived), Pressure = force/area (derived).

title: The SI System — International System of Units

sections.heading: What is SI?
sections.body:
SI stands for Système International d'Unités (International System of Units). It was established in 1960 by the General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM).

It is the globally accepted standard system of units used in science and engineering.

sections.heading: Why SI?
sections.body:
Before SI, different countries used different systems:
• CGS (centimetre-gram-second)
• FPS (foot-pound-second)
• MKS (metre-kilogram-second)

SI unified everything. It is based on the MKS system but extended with 4 more base units.

highlight: JEE problems always use SI units unless explicitly stated otherwise. If a problem gives values in CGS, convert to SI first!

title: The 7 SI Base Units — Memorize This Table

sections.heading: The Sacred Seven
sections.body:
1. Length → metre (m)
2. Mass → kilogram (kg)
3. Time → second (s)
4. Electric Current → ampere (A)
5. Temperature → kelvin (K)
6. Amount of Substance → mole (mol)
7. Luminous Intensity → candela (cd)

sections.heading: Key Details
sections.body:
• kilogram is the ONLY base unit with a prefix (kilo-). The base unit is kg, NOT gram.
• Temperature in SI is kelvin, NOT Celsius. K = °C + 273.15
• The mole connects the atomic world to the macroscopic world: 1 mol = 6.022 × 10²³ entities.

highlight: Memory trick: "Little Monkeys Travel Every Thursday Morning Carefully" → Length, Mass, Time, Electric current, Temperature, (a)Mount of substance, Candela

question: Which of the following is the SI base unit of temperature?
explanation: Kelvin is the SI base unit for thermodynamic temperature. Celsius is widely used but is NOT the SI base unit. K = °C + 273.15.

instruction: Match each fundamental quantity to its SI unit:
explanation: These 5 (along with mole and candela) form the 7 SI base units. Every other unit in physics is derived from combinations of these.

title: How Are SI Base Units Defined? (2019 Redefinitions)

sections.heading: Modern Definitions (JEE Aware)
sections.body:
Since 2019, all SI units are defined using fundamental physical constants:

• metre — defined by fixing the speed of light: c = 299,792,458 m/s exactly
• kilogram — defined by fixing Planck's constant: h = 6.62607015 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s
• second — defined by cesium-133 atom: 9,192,631,770 oscillations = 1 second
• ampere — defined by fixing elementary charge: e = 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C
• kelvin — defined by fixing Boltzmann constant: k = 1.380649 × 10⁻²³ J/K

sections.heading: Why This Matters for JEE
sections.body:
JEE occasionally asks about the definition of metre or second. Remember:
• 1 metre = distance light travels in 1/299,792,458 seconds
• 1 second = 9,192,631,770 periods of cesium-133 radiation

highlight: The kilogram is NO LONGER defined by a physical prototype. Since 2019, it's defined using Planck's constant.

question: The SI unit of length (metre) is currently defined in terms of:
options: A platinum-iridium bar kept in Paris
Distance between two marks on a metal rod
explanation: Since 1983, 1 metre = distance light travels in vacuum in 1/299,792,458 seconds. The krypton-86 definition was used from 1960–1983. The platinum-iridium bar was the original definition (1889).

title: Supplementary & Derived Units

sections.heading: Two Supplementary Units (now within SI)
sections.body:
• Plane Angle → radian (rad) — angle subtended by an arc equal in length to the radius
• Solid Angle → steradian (sr) — solid angle subtended at the centre of a sphere by a surface area equal to r²

Note: These were reclassified as 'dimensionless derived units' in 1995, but JEE still references them.

sections.heading: Derived Units — Examples
sections.body:
Every other unit is built from the 7 base units:
• Newton (N) = kg·m·s⁻²
• Joule (J) = kg·m²·s⁻²
• Watt (W) = kg·m²·s⁻³
• Pascal (Pa) = kg·m⁻¹·s⁻²
• Coulomb (C) = A·s
• Volt (V) = kg·m²·s⁻³·A⁻¹

highlight: Every formula in physics is ultimately expressible in terms of kg, m, s, A, K, mol, cd.

question: The SI unit of force (Newton) expressed in base units is:
explanation:
Force = mass × acceleration = kg × (m/s²) = kg·m·s⁻². This is 1 Newton.

kg·m·s⁻¹ would be momentum. kg·m²·s⁻² would be energy (Joule).

sentence: The SI unit of energy (Joule) expressed in base units is _______.
explanation:
Energy = Force × Distance = (kg·m·s⁻²) × m = kg·m²·s⁻²

Note: kg·m·s⁻² = Newton (force), kg·m²·s⁻³ = Watt (power), kg·m⁻¹·s⁻² = Pascal (pressure).
hint: Energy = Force × Distance. What's Force in base units?

title: SI Prefixes — Powers of 10

sections.heading: Common Prefixes for JEE
sections.body:
Large:
• kilo (k) = 10³
• mega (M) = 10⁶
• giga (G) = 10⁹
• tera (T) = 10¹²

Small:
• milli (m) = 10⁻³
• micro (μ) = 10⁻⁶
• nano (n) = 10⁻⁹
• pico (p) = 10⁻¹²
• femto (f) = 10⁻¹⁵
• angstrom (Å) = 10⁻¹⁰ m (not an SI prefix but commonly used)

sections.heading: Converting with Prefixes
sections.body:
To convert: replace the prefix with its power of 10.

5.2 km = 5.2 × 10³ m = 5200 m
3.7 μs = 3.7 × 10⁻⁶ s
15 nm = 15 × 10⁻⁹ m = 1.5 × 10⁻⁸ m

highlight: 1 Å (angstrom) = 10⁻¹⁰ m = 0.1 nm. Atomic radii are typically 1–3 Å.

question: 1 nanometre (nm) is equal to:
explanation:
The prefix 'nano' means 10⁻⁹. So 1 nm = 10⁻⁹ m.

10⁻⁶ m = 1 micrometre (μm), 10⁻¹⁰ m = 1 angstrom (Å), 10⁻¹² m = 1 picometre (pm).

instruction: Match each SI prefix to its power of 10:
explanation: Notice the pattern: mega/micro are ±6, giga/nano are ±9, tera/pico are ±12. The large and small prefixes mirror each other!

title: Other Systems of Units (CGS, FPS, Natural)

sections.heading: CGS System
sections.body:
Base units: centimetre (cm), gram (g), second (s)

Still used in some areas of physics. Key conversions:
• 1 m = 100 cm
• 1 kg = 1000 g
• 1 N = 10⁵ dyne (CGS unit of force)
• 1 J = 10⁷ erg (CGS unit of energy)

sections.heading: Natural Units & Planck Units
sections.body:
In theoretical physics, natural units set c = ℏ = 1.

Planck units (JEE rarely asks, but good to know):
• Planck length = √(ℏG/c³) ≈ 1.6 × 10⁻³⁵ m
• Planck time = √(ℏG/c⁵) ≈ 5.4 × 10⁻⁴⁴ s
• Planck mass = √(ℏc/G) ≈ 2.2 × 10⁻⁸ kg

highlight: CGS conversions appear in JEE: 1 N = 10⁵ dyne, 1 J = 10⁷ erg. Memorize these!

question: 1 Newton is equal to how many dynes?
explanation:
1 N = 1 kg·m·s⁻²
1 kg = 10³ g, 1 m = 10² cm
So 1 N = 10³ g × 10² cm × s⁻² = 10⁵ g·cm·s⁻² = 10⁵ dyne
hint: Convert kg to grams and metres to centimetres separately, then multiply.

title: Dimensions of Physical Quantities

sections.heading: What are Dimensions?
sections.body:
Dimensions express a physical quantity in terms of the fundamental quantities using symbols:

[M] = Mass, [L] = Length, [T] = Time
[A] = Current, [K] = Temperature
[mol] = Amount, [cd] = Luminous Intensity

The dimensional formula tells you HOW a quantity is built from fundamentals.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.body:
• Velocity = Length/Time → [L T⁻¹]
• Acceleration = Velocity/Time → [L T⁻²]
• Force = Mass × Acceleration → [M L T⁻²]
• Energy = Force × Distance → [M L² T⁻²]
• Pressure = Force / Area → [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]
• Power = Energy / Time → [M L² T⁻³]

highlight: To find dimensions: write the formula, substitute base dimensions, simplify. This works for ANY quantity.

question: The dimensional formula of momentum is:
explanation:
Momentum = mass × velocity = M × [L T⁻¹] = [M L T⁻¹]

[M L T⁻²] = Force, [M L² T⁻¹] = Angular momentum, [M L² T⁻²] = Energy

sentence: The dimensional formula of Planck's constant (h) is _______.
explanation:
E = hν → h = E/ν
Dimension of E = [M L² T⁻²], dimension of ν (frequency) = [T⁻¹]
h = [M L² T⁻²] / [T⁻¹] = [M L² T⁻¹]

Note: This is the same dimension as angular momentum!
hint: Use E = hν. Find dimensions of E and frequency separately.

title: ⚡ Dimensionless Quantities
body:
Some quantities have NO dimensions — all base dimensions cancel out. Examples:

• Angle (radian) = arc/radius = [L]/[L] = dimensionless
• Strain = ΔL/L = dimensionless
• Refractive index = c/v = dimensionless
• Relative density = ρ_substance/ρ_water = dimensionless

quick.label: Dimensionless ≠ unitless. Angle is dimensionless but has unit 'radian'
Pure numbers, ratios, and trigonometric values are dimensionless
Logarithmic, exponential arguments must be dimensionless

question: Which of the following quantities is NOT dimensionless?
explanation:
Angular velocity (ω) = angle/time = rad/s. Its dimension is [T⁻¹] — NOT dimensionless.

Strain = ΔL/L = [L]/[L] = dimensionless
Angle = arc/radius = [L]/[L] = dimensionless
Refractive index = c/v = [LT⁻¹]/[LT⁻¹] = dimensionless

title: Dimensional Analysis — The Power Tool

sections.heading: Principle of Homogeneity
sections.body:
In any valid physics equation, every term must have the SAME dimensions.

If s = ut + ½at², then:
• [s] = [L]
• [ut] = [LT⁻¹][T] = [L] ✓
• [½at²] = [LT⁻²][T²] = [L] ✓

All terms have dimension [L]. The equation is dimensionally consistent.

sections.heading: Three Uses of Dimensional Analysis
sections.body:
1. Checking correctness of equations
2. Deriving relationships between quantities
3. Converting units between systems (SI ↔ CGS)

highlight: Dimensional analysis can verify an equation but CANNOT determine dimensionless constants (like ½, π, 2π).

question: The equation v = u + at² is dimensionally:
explanation:
[v] = [LT⁻¹], [u] = [LT⁻¹] ✓
[at²] = [LT⁻²][T²] = [L] ✗

[L] ≠ [LT⁻¹], so the equation is dimensionally incorrect.
The correct equation is v = u + at (not at²).

title: Deriving Formulas Using Dimensional Analysis

sections.heading: The Method
sections.body:
If a quantity Q depends on quantities a, b, c, assume:
Q = k · aˣ · bʸ · cᶻ

where k is a dimensionless constant.

Write dimensions of both sides, compare powers of M, L, T to find x, y, z.

sections.heading: Example: Time period of a simple pendulum
sections.body:
T depends on: length (l), mass (m), acceleration due to gravity (g).
Assume: T = k · lˣ · mʸ · gᶻ

Dimensions:
[T] = [L]ˣ · [M]ʸ · [LT⁻²]ᶻ
[M⁰ L⁰ T¹] = [Mʸ · Lˣ⁺ᶻ · T⁻²ᶻ]

Comparing:
M: y = 0 → period is independent of mass!
T: -2z = 1 → z = -½
L: x + z = 0 → x = ½

So T = k · l^(1/2) · g^(-1/2) = k√(l/g)
Actual formula: T = 2π√(l/g). Dimensional analysis gives everything except 2π.

highlight: Dimensional analysis CANNOT find pure numbers like 2π, ½, etc. It only gives the functional dependence.

question: If the velocity of a wave (v) depends on tension (T) and linear mass density (μ), then v is proportional to:
explanation:
v = k · Tˣ · μʸ
[LT⁻¹] = [MLT⁻²]ˣ · [ML⁻¹]ʸ

M: x + y = 0
L: x − y = 1
T: −2x = −1 → x = ½

From x + y = 0: y = −½

So v = k · T^(1/2) · μ^(-1/2) = k√(T/μ)
Actual formula: v = √(T/μ)
hint: Tension has units of force [MLT⁻²]. Linear mass density has units [ML⁻¹].

title: Unit Conversion Using Dimensions

sections.heading: The Formula
sections.body:
To convert a quantity from one system to another:

n₂ = n₁ × (M₁/M₂)ᵃ × (L₁/L₂)ᵇ × (T₁/T₂)ᶜ

where [Mᵃ Lᵇ Tᶜ] is the dimensional formula, and subscripts 1, 2 refer to the two systems.

highlight: This method works for converting ANY quantity between ANY two unit systems. Just know the dimensional formula.

question: Convert 1 Newton to CGS system using dimensional analysis:
explanation:
Force = [M L T⁻²]
1 N = 1 × (1kg/1g)¹ × (1m/1cm)¹ × (1s/1s)⁻²
     = (10³)¹ × (10²)¹ × 1
     = 10³ × 10² = 10⁵ dyne

title: 🧠 Limitations of Dimensional Analysis
body: Dimensional analysis is powerful but has clear limitations you must know for JEE:

quick.label: Cannot determine dimensionless constants (½, π, e, etc.)
Cannot derive formulas involving addition/subtraction of quantities
Cannot distinguish between quantities with same dimensions (work vs torque)
Cannot derive relations involving trig, log, or exponential functions
Works only when the relation is a power-law (product of powers)

title: Spot the Error: Dimensional Analysis
instruction: One of these statements is WRONG. Which one?

sentences.text: A dimensionally correct equation may not be physically correct.
A dimensionally incorrect equation is always physically wrong.
Dimensional analysis can be used to derive the exact formula for centripetal force, including the constant.
sentences.explanation: WRONG. Dimensional analysis gives F ∝ mv²/r, but cannot determine that the constant is exactly 1. It can give the functional form but never dimensionless constants. The fact that F = mv²/r (with constant = 1) must be derived from Newton's laws.

title: Important Dimensional Formulae for JEE

sections.heading: Quantities with SAME Dimensions (JEE Trap!)
sections.body:
These groups share identical dimensions:

• Work, Energy, Torque → [M L² T⁻²]
• Pressure, Stress, Young's Modulus → [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]
• Angular momentum, Planck's constant → [M L² T⁻¹]
• Force, Impulse/time → [M L T⁻²]
• Frequency, Angular velocity, Velocity gradient, Decay constant → [T⁻¹]

sections.heading: Tricky Ones
sections.body:
• Gravitational constant G → [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²] (from F = GMm/r²)
• Boltzmann constant k → [M L² T⁻² K⁻¹] (same as R/Nₐ)
• Stefan's constant σ → [M T⁻³ K⁻⁴] (from P/A = σT⁴)
• Permittivity ε₀ → [M⁻¹ L⁻³ T⁴ A²] (from Coulomb's law)

highlight: JEE loves asking: 'Which pair has the same dimensions?' → Work & Torque, Pressure & Stress, Angular momentum & Planck's constant.

question: Which pair of quantities has the SAME dimensional formula?
explanation:
Angular momentum (L = mvr) → [M][LT⁻¹][L] = [M L² T⁻¹]
Planck's constant (h = E/ν) → [ML²T⁻²]/[T⁻¹] = [M L² T⁻¹] ✓ Same!

Work = [ML²T⁻²], Power = [ML²T⁻³] → different
Force = [MLT⁻²], Impulse = [MLT⁻¹] → different

instruction: Arrange these derived units from SMALLEST to LARGEST dimension of length (power of L):
explanation:
Power of L: Pressure has L⁻¹, Force has L¹, Energy has L², Power has L².
Since -1 < 1 < 2 = 2, the order is: Pressure < Force < Energy = Power.
(Energy and Power both have L², so either order works for the last two.)
hint: Look at the exponent of L in each dimensional formula.

question: The dimensional formula of the universal gravitational constant G is:
explanation:
From F = GMm/r² → G = Fr²/(Mm)
[G] = [MLT⁻²][L²] / ([M][M]) = [ML³T⁻²] / [M²] = [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²]
hint: Rearrange F = GMm/r² to solve for G, then substitute dimensions.

question: A physical quantity X is defined as X = (3kT)/(μv²), where k is Boltzmann constant, T is temperature, μ is a mass, and v is velocity. X is dimensionally equivalent to:
explanation:
[kT] = [ML²T⁻²K⁻¹][K] = [ML²T⁻²] (this is energy)
[μv²] = [M][LT⁻¹]² = [M][L²T⁻²] = [ML²T⁻²] (also energy)

[X] = [ML²T⁻²] / [ML²T⁻²] = [M⁰L⁰T⁰] = dimensionless

The constant 3 is also dimensionless. X is a pure ratio.
hint: kT has dimensions of energy. What about μv²?

meaning: A method to check equations, derive relations, and convert units by comparing dimensions [M, L, T, A, K] on both sides.
wrong: Cannot find dimensionless constants (π, ½). Cannot work with trig/log/exponential functions.
family: Fundamental quantities — M, L, T, A, K, mol, cd
Derived quantities — velocity, force, energy, etc.

title: 🏁 Chapter Summary — SI Units & Dimensions

sections.heading: Key Takeaways
sections.body:
1. There are 7 SI base units: m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd
2. All other units are derived from these 7
3. Every quantity has a dimensional formula using [M, L, T, A, K]
4. Dimensional analysis can check formulas, derive relations, convert units
5. It CANNOT find dimensionless constants or handle trig/log functions

sections.heading: Most Important for JEE
sections.body:
• Know: 7 base units and their definitions (especially metre, second)
• Know: dimensional formulae of common quantities
• Know: same-dimension pairs (Work=Torque, Angular momentum=Planck's constant)
• Practice: deriving formulas and converting between SI and CGS
• Remember: 1 N = 10⁵ dyne, 1 J = 10⁷ erg

highlight: You've covered the complete JEE syllabus for SI Units, Fundamental vs Derived quantities, and Dimensional Analysis. Next up: Errors, Significant Figures, and Precision!

question: If E, m, l, and G denote energy, mass, angular momentum, and gravitational constant respectively, then the dimensions of El²/(m⁵G²) are:
explanation:
[E] = [ML²T⁻²]
[l] = [ML²T⁻¹] (angular momentum)
[G] = [M⁻¹L³T⁻²]

[El²] = [ML²T⁻²][ML²T⁻¹]² = [ML²T⁻²][M²L⁴T⁻²] = [M³L⁶T⁻⁴]

[m⁵G²] = [M⁵][M⁻¹L³T⁻²]² = [M⁵][M⁻²L⁶T⁻⁴] = [M³L⁶T⁻⁴]

[El²/(m⁵G²)] = [M³L⁶T⁻⁴]/[M³L⁶T⁻⁴] = [M⁰L⁰T⁰] → dimensionless!
hint: Write out all dimensions carefully. It helps to compute numerator and denominator separately.
